back: When everyone has the same chances in an education system, regardless of their background.
Selective schooling uses exams for entry; comprehensive schooling is for everyone and does not require entrance exams.
When a small, privileged group is favored within the education system.
Lists of schools or colleges that rank them from the best down to the worst based on performance.
A system that has two separate levels, one of which is considered better than the other.
Schools that receive a significant amount of money through grants, gifts, or private funding.
To achieve an excellent standard in academic or other work.
The traditional basic skills of reading, writing, and arithmetic (maths).
'Literacy' is the ability to read, while 'numeracy' is the ability to count and do basic maths.
Education provided for people of all ages, including mature students who are older than the average student.
A teacher who works in different schools and travels between them to provide specialized instruction.
To make unfair situations or social differences continue for a long time.
